sources: production/cloud-week/sound/manifest.json and sources.json (97 files, 46 CC0 sources, rebuilt by make_sound.py)
RULINGS.md 24 Nov (no thinking sound), 1 Oct, 5 Oct
canon.md (content rule, fictional brands, the brand bible owes the pirate station)
production/lane/blueprint/data/content-words.json (content check run over this file's text)
open_points: Setts have no recording (cloud-week NOTES): step_setts is a stone patio and old slabs, the nearest hard stone. Wet steps are the weakest set. The cloud week's own caution stands: nobody has heard any of the 97 files in the game; the listening pass (MEASUREMENTS-NEEDED A7) has not been done.

The three voices-through-a-window and radio loops (amb_voices_*, amb_radio_*) are cut from speech recordings: they need the content check (no word, no child's voice, nothing about drink or gambling) before shipping; the cloud-week notes say that listening has not happened.

Rule files: the sound reach of each deed (how far a step, door, shot is heard) is in tune.json under the keys listed in reach_keys; this file only names the key. The one function here is the footstep loudness = reach in metres / 10.

Evening sound state starts at the lamp strike when that is before 18:00 (chosen) so the sound follows the light file: sunset is about 15:46 on 30 Nov, when a fixed 18:00 would leave the street 'day' for two dark hours.
Drizzle far-voice cap is a floor of three quarters and rain a floor of half (chosen); SND-02 gives only 'halves the far voices allowed' for rain.

Synthesis recipes are specifications for the one-shot's Web Audio code (noise, oscillators, filters, envelopes), not tested sounds; every level target marked chosen is a guess to be set by ear. Voices (shouts, pain cries) are voice-tool lines; recipes are test stand-ins only.
The kiosk payphone ring: no recording was found; the GPO house phone stands in (cloud-week NOTES).
Milk float, paper round and the curtain answer (catalogue 23 Nov, rank 10) are not in the blueprint; two are listed so the one-shot may build them; they may be cut.

The pirate station name 'Cutter FM', its presenters and programme grid are chosen here (the brand bible owes the station). All names are fictional; they have not been run through tools/brand-verify.py.

The tune melodies are generated from fixed seeds and never compared with any real tune; a resemblance by chance is unlikely but nobody has listened. A rendering pass with the allowlist's item 5 tool is optional and waits for the radio production start.
RULINGS 24 Nov: no thinking sound before a talk answer. The 28 Sep line asking for a short thinking sound is dropped: no such cue is in this file. The cab radio squelch plays only on a radio call.

Prototype gull and ship's horn intervals (every 55 to 140 s real) were set on the 45 s hour; on the 120 s hour the horn interval is 27 to 70 game minutes (about 54 to 140 real seconds, so the same real-time rate); old 55 to 140 s, new 54 to 140 s real.
The pirate station was minted twice in parallel (Slack Tide FM here, Cutter FM in letters-and-print.json); letters-and-print.json is the brand list, so Cutter FM is used here too.

Small hours are 00:00 to 05:00 in both files (decision 24 Nov): early state 05:00 to 08:00, evening 18:00 to 24:00; the sound plan's 23:00 to 05:30 is superseded. Rain's effect on reach is the single figure tune:noise.rain_factor (0.6 rain, 0.8 drizzle) in tune.json.
Hour reach: one scheme in tune.json; this file holds no reach multiplier.
Tune titles are checked only from recall; run a title search before shipping.
Tom's 16 step files are in production/assets/steps, outside the cloud-week manifest; added to files with CC0 licence from research/footsteps/NOTE-2026-09-30.md (checked 30 Sep 2026).

lines.text: Cutter FM, on the air when the aerial's up.
You're listening to Cutter FM, the station that moves when the tide does.
This is Cutter FM. If it's crackling, that's the weather, not us.
Morning, quay. First Light on the Tide, and it's wet out there, so keep your collars up.
Seven minutes past six, the dock shift's on, and here's Lamp Light Walk from the Leadlights.
The ferry's running on time, which is news in itself.
High water at ten to eight. Mind the steps by the basin.
Dot here, and it's dinner time on the Hook. Ring in if you've a name to send a tune to.
This one goes out to the Washeteria on Quay Street. Those machines have been turning since eight.
A dedication for the night shift on the fish dock, from someone who says you know who you are.
A bit of Ropewalk Rain for the lady on Chapel Lane who rang in twice.
Ring the box on the parade if you've something to say, but be quick, the signal wanders.
Teatime Tide, and the lamps are on along the quay. For anyone making their way home.
North Road's slow tonight. Allow ten minutes.
If you're heading to the match, the quay will be quiet by half past five. Mind the wet.
Mal Rudge, Slack Water Sessions. The line's open. Well, one line is, and it's not a good one.
Caller, you're on Cutter FM. Go ahead, and mind your language.
That was Fog Signal from Quiet Ferris. If you've not had your tea, the chip shop on the parade is open until half eleven.
It's gone eleven. If you're out, get yourself in, and if you're in, stay in.
Last tune of the night, then I'm off before the signal does.
That's Cutter FM away till morning. Keep the aerial straight.
Weather: grey, with more grey later.
Drizzle on the Hook, and not a lot else.
Rain on the quay. I'd tell you to bring a coat, but you've already got it on.
We've lost a bit of signal. If you can still hear me, you've a better aerial than I have.

dead_air.plays_when: a radio is tuned to Cutter FM and it is off air (01:00 to 05:30) or lost to signal

radio.speech_rule: radio_speech lines are played through the source's filter as voice-tool speech by fictional presenters (made like any other voice, SND-22); a link plays between tunes by the programme's link_every_n_tunes; weather lines match the current profile; a live programme may drop a line for 'rl_lost' for 20 s at random 1 time in 6 hours (chosen)
radio.tune_choice: next tune is the next in the programme's tune_pool, wrapping; a tune loops from its beginning if the player stays near; start offset is seeded by game day so the same seed gives the same radio

reach_key_map_suggested.note: this file names reach keys as tune:sound.reach.*, as the brief says. tune.json (built in parallel) names its figures differently; where one is plainly the same figure it is listed here. Keys with no entry (horn, car, siren, snooker, boxing, pigeon and so on) have no tune.json figure yet and should be added there or taken from the sound plan (car 44 m, horn 60 m, shot 177 m by day).
